top_choice_rationale: P001 recognises a new measurement concept: magic-wavelength trapping cancels the light shift while Doppler and recoil shifts are removed, so thousands of neutral atoms are interrogated in parallel. It was demonstrated experimentally, reproduced and surpassed at the 10^-18 level in independent laboratories, and the two-name allocation (Katori for the proposal and first strontium realisation, Ye for the accuracy frontier) is compact and the citation is scoped to the lattice idea, not to the comb or ion control already honoured in 2005 and 2012. P002 is a sound, mature prediction-plus-experiment chain, but it follows the 2016 topological prize closely and leaves credit questions (Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, Hasan). I prefer awarding it to no award.
recusal_note: Distant mentor-lineage link: I spent a year in John Hall's laboratory during my PhD, and Hall's JILA group is the lineage in which Jun Ye worked; no direct collaboration with Ye or Katori. Not a conflict requiring recusal in my view, but disclosed. Ballot completed regardless.
